title: Set up and check an airflow simulation with an agent
summary: Navier's engineering agent set up, ran and checked a high-speed airflow simulation of a grid fin; the team reports the shock angle landed within 0.04° of theory.
agent_role: The agent set up the simulation, ran it and validated the results; the team chose the test case.
outcome: Navier reports the shock angle came within 0.04° of textbook oblique-shock theory.
what_they_did: The Navier team gave its engineering agent, in their Prism product, a grid fin test case. Grid fins are lattice-shaped control surfaces used on rockets. The agent set up a high-speed airflow simulation in OpenFOAM, a free simulation tool, then ran and checked it.
how_it_went: The team says the predicted shock angle landed within 0.04° of the value from standard theory. They say the agent keeps holding up as they test more kinds of physics.
worth_knowing: This comes from the company that makes the agent, with no files or details shared.
prompt: Set up an OpenFOAM simulation of [describe shape] in high-speed airflow at [speed or Mach number]. Show me your plan first: mesh, solver, boundary conditions and run time. After I approve, run it, then compare a key result such as [shock angle] against the textbook theory value and report the difference.

curation.rationale: Genuine engineering agent that set up, ran and checked a fluid simulation with a concrete accuracy number, but very thin and promotional for the company's own product.
